I recommend `AGENTS.md` + a `$docs-audit` skill + a Codex `Stop` hook. Do not use `SessionEnd` for the audit.

1. Audit result

In 11 locally retained Entire transcripts:

- 0 used DeepWiki.
- 8 read local project documentation.
- 5 explicitly reported a documentation outcome.
- All four recorded Codex implementation sessions reported one.

Remote Entire search was unavailable because the CLI is not logged in. This is a local-history sample.

2. Recommended documentation loop

- `AGENTS.md` defines which documents own each product surface.
- `$docs-audit` defines how to compare the completed diff.
- A `Stop` hook invokes `$docs-audit` after file edits.
- CI checks that PRs include a documentation result.

I prefer `$docs-audit` over `$session-end`. “Session end” now names an actual Codex lifecycle event.

A skill alone is not guaranteed. Codex initially sees only its description and decides whether to load it. `AGENTS.md` is loaded before work, but remains an instruction rather than enforcement. [OpenAI skills documentation](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/build-skills), [AGENTS.md documentation](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-configuration/agents-md).

3. Why `Stop`, not `SessionEnd`

A Codex `Stop` hook can continue the current agent turn with this instruction:

> Run `$docs-audit`. Update affected docs, then report the documentation result.

`SessionEnd` happens after closing, archiving, deleting, or 30 minutes of inactivity. Its output cannot steer Codex or keep the thread open. [OpenAI hooks documentation](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/hooks).

The skill should require:

- Inspect this session’s completed diff.
- Map changes through the `AGENTS.md` docs list.
- Update incorrect or incomplete documents.
- Preserve unrelated dirty work.
- Finish with `Docs: updated …` or a specific no-change reason.

4. DeepWiki

DeepWiki should be a navigation aid, not your documentation source of truth.

Your current [Devin MCP guidance](/Users/lorenzkrinner/Dev/hackathons/ehl_hack/docs/agents/devin-mcp.md) already says local files take precedence. I would only strengthen its trigger:

> For broad architecture or unfamiliar modules, query Devin Wiki, then verify against the current branch.

DeepWiki indexes connected repositories during Devin onboarding. For public repositories, Cognition says a DeepWiki badge enables automatic refreshes. However, official documentation does not publish an exact refresh interval. It also describes manual regeneration. Therefore, do not assume a push updates the Wiki immediately. [DeepWiki documentation](https://docs.devin.ai/work-with-devin/deepwiki), [official DeepWiki repository](https://github.com/CognitionAI/deepwiki).

No files were changed. Estimated setup time: 20–30 minutes.
